mainEntity.name: What does a crypto exchange PR agency actually do?

acceptedAnswer.text: Exchange PR covers four distinct workstreams: listing announcements timed to maximise tier-1 pick-up, security and compliance positioning that builds institutional trust before it is needed, regional market entry comms across APAC and MENA, and crisis readiness so a breach or regulatory inquiry does not become a reputational spiral. Shilika Jain runs all four directly at $5K–$12K/month.

mainEntity.name: How much does crypto exchange PR cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Traditional agencies price exchange retainers at $15K–$45K/month because the fee supports a multi-person account team. A fractional senior operator delivers the same senior scope for $5K–$12K/month, and a targeted listing sprint runs $15K–$40K over four to eight weeks. KOL amplification adds cost depending on tier: nano creators run $200–$1.5K per placement, micro $500–$5K, mid-tier $10K–$30K and macro $25K–$100K or more.

mainEntity.name: Which outlets can you secure for an exchange?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tier-1 crypto: CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, The Block, Decrypt, Blockworks, The Defiant. Mainstream finance where the angle warrants it: Forbes, Bloomberg, Yahoo Finance, Benzinga. Regional exchange beats: BloomingBit and TokenPost (Korea), CryptoTimes JP and CoinPost (Japan), ChainCatcher and Jinse (China), Inc42 (India), e27 (SEA), and Gulf News and Zawya for MENA. Placement depends on a real news hook: a listing with genuine liquidity, a compliance milestone, or a verifiable security audit.

mainEntity.name: What does the crisis communications process look like?

acceptedAnswer.text: Crisis prep begins in the first two weeks: we map the three most likely incident types for your exchange, draft pre-approved response templates, set up a rapid-response communication chain, and agree on a spokesperson protocol. When an incident occurs, the goal is a factual first statement within two hours.
